shippingNews.postTitle: R/V Neil Armstrong Expected in Duluth Nov. 9

stories.body: The R/V Neil Armstrong, which departed its home port of Woods Hole, Massachusetts, on Wednesday, October 28, is expected to arrive in Duluth on November 9 after passing through the Welland Canal on Thursday. The University of Minnesota Duluth is working with the research vessel to detect and observe neutrino interactions in Lake Superior. Neutrinos are the most abundant particles that have mass in the universe, and they pass through everything. They are very difficult to detect, so studying them requires special instruments. shippingNews.postTitle: Tug William Eugene Makes First Trip to Saginaw River

stories.body: Tug William Eugene on the Saginaw River. [Todd Shorkey] The Stasinos Marine tug William Eugene arrived on the Saginaw River Tuesday morning, making the turn into the slip at Port Fisher and tied up there. William Eugene used to be the Malcolm Marine tug, Capt. Keith and this is believed to be her first time on the Saginaw River. Photos taken 11/3/26. Todd Shorkey

todayInHistory.title: Fire Causes Significant Damage to Two Harbors Lighthouse Gift Shop
todayInHistory.text: TWO HARBORS, MN – An investigation is underway after a detached building that’s used as a gift shop for the Two Harbors Lighthouse went up in flames Monday evening. As of Tuesday morning, local authorities have yet to release information on the blaze, which likely broke out around 5:30 p.m. Officials with the Lake County Historical Society, which controls the lakeside property, told Northern News Now that no one was injured, but the damage to the building is significant. “We were literally watching a piece of Lake County’s history go up in those flames,” Lake County Historical Society Vice President David Johnson said in an interview with the station. It’s believed that the fire started in the breezeway between the gift shop and a connected structure, both of which are separate from the historic lighthouse. The Lake County Historical Society shared this statement: “We are incredibly grateful to the firefighters and first responders who have responded and are working to address the situation. Their time, dedication, and efforts are greatly appreciated.” Bring Me The News Gift shop fire at Two Harbors Lighthouse.

marineWeather.synopsis: This morning, a 30.3 inch high extends from northern Ontario to the Texas Panhandle while a 29.7 inch low moves over Labrador and extends surface troughing south across New England. Through tonight, the high will split, with a 30.3 inch high over Quebec and a 30.2 inch high over Missouri leaving 30.1 inch remnant ridging over the lake. Meanwhile, the main low will move offshore but the troughing will consolidate into a 29.8 inch low over Massachusetts. Through Saturday, pressure begins to fall over Lake Superior as a 29.5 inch low moves off the Canadian Rockies and into northern Manitoba. This low moves into northern Ontario Saturday night into Sunday, passing 29.7 inch troughing over the lake. With the low moving to the mouth of the St Lawrence at 29.3 inches Sunday night, weak ridging of around 30.0 inches moves over Lake Superior associated with 30.2 inch high pressure over Texas. By Monday morning, a 29.5 inch low will move over Lake Winnipeg, weakening to 29.7 inches as if moves near or over the lake Monday night. Tuesday through Wednesday, this low shifts east as 30.4 inch high pressure builds over the Manitoba/Ontario line.

Breezy northerly winds continue as a tight pressure gradient remains over Lake Michigan between low pressure of 29.8 inches over Lake Huron and high pressure of 30.3 inches over the northern Plains. Northerly gales around 35 kt are expected to linger through this afternoon as the pressure gradient remains over the lake, and a Gale Warning remains in effect. Winds will diminish from north to south this afternoon. Middle and southern portions of the lake will continue to see waterspout potential through this afternoon as well. High pressure then builds over the Upper Great Lakes this afternoon through the weekend, bringing lighter northwesterly winds. Low pressure around 29.4 inches crossing Ontario will drag a weak cold front across Lake Michigan on Sunday. Highest gusts up to 30 kt are expected over the north half. The next low pressure system will cross Lake Superior Monday night.
marineWeather.warning: GALE WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 PM CST THIS EVENING

marineWeather.synopsis: A low pressure system will close off over central Lake Huron today around 29.70 inches. This will lead to a period of strong northerly winds over Lake Huron today and into Saturday as the low drifts slowly southward.

A cold front will swing east across the lake this morning before a trough averaging 29.90 inches will linger across the lake through Saturday. A ridge averaging 30.10 inches will build over the lake Saturday night through Sunday. Another cold front will sweep southeast across the lake Sunday night with a trough averaging 30.00 inches persisting early next week.

A trough averaging 29.8 inches will impact the eastern Great Lakes through this weekend and into early next week. However, a narrow ridge of high pressure averaging 30.0 inches will move eastward across the eastern Great Lakes Saturday night. Another ridge averaging 30.0 inches should move eastward across the eastern Great Lakes later Monday through Monday night. A trough averaging 29.8 inches from a passing cold front will cross the region Tuesday.
